title: Nephi Begins His Record
summary: Nephi introduces his record, its language, and his confidence in its truth.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he was born of goodly parents, taught in his father’s learning, experienced afflictions, and was favored by the Lord.
Nephi says he makes a record of his proceedings.
He describes the record’s language as consisting of the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians.
Nephi says the record is true, made with his own hand according to his knowledge.

unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s age, clothing, appearance, and exact place of writing.

narration.text: I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents
I make a record in the language of my father
I know that the record which I make is true

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi’s parents; they are not shown in these verses.

title: Prophets Warn Jerusalem
summary: In the first year of Zedekiah’s reign, many prophets preach repentance and warn that Jerusalem will be destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: At the commencement of Zedekiah’s first year as king of Judah, many prophets tell the people to repent or Jerusalem will be destroyed.
Lehi had dwelt at Jerusalem all his days.

unspecified_visual_details: The prophets’ identities, appearances, number, and exact location within Jerusalem.

narration.text: they must repent
the great city Jerusalem must be destroyed

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Zedekiah as present; the verse only dates the events by his reign.

title: Lehi Prays for His People
summary: Lehi goes forth and prays to the Lord with all his heart on behalf of his people.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi goes forth and prays to the Lord with all his heart for his people.

unspecified_visual_details: Exact prayer location, posture, clothing, and surroundings.

narration.text: my father, Lehi, as he went forth prayed unto the Lord

summary: As Lehi prays, a pillar of fire rests on a rock before him; he sees and hears much and trembles.

explicit_facts.text: As Lehi prays, a pillar of fire comes and rests upon a rock before him.
Lehi sees and hears much and quakes and trembles exceedingly because of what he sees and hears.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi returns to his own house at Jerusalem and casts himself upon his bed, overcome with the Spirit and the things he had seen.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi on a bed inside his house.

title: The Heavens Open
summary: In a vision, Lehi sees the heavens open and thinks he sees God seated on a throne amid numberless angels singing and praising.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi is carried away in a vision and sees the heavens open.
He thinks he sees God seated upon a throne, surrounded by numberless concourses of angels in an attitude of singing and praising God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: God seated on a throne and angels in an attitude of praise, as seen in Lehi’s vision.
unspecified_visual_details: God’s appearance, the angels’ individual appearances, and the nature of their singing.

title: One Descends from Heaven
summary: Lehi sees One descend from heaven, brighter than the sun at noon, followed by twelve others brighter than the stars.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi sees One descending from the midst of heaven, whose luster is above that of the sun at noon.
Lehi sees twelve others following, whose brightness exceeds that of the stars in the firmament.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The One and the twelve others are luminous as described.
unspecified_visual_details: Their identities, faces, clothing, and other attributes.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is presented as a vision seen by Lehi.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the One or the twelve.

title: The Book Is Given
summary: The figures come down and go upon the earth; the first stands before Lehi, gives him a book, and bids him read.

explicit_facts.text: The figures come down and go forth upon the face of the earth.
The first comes and stands before Lehi, gives him a book, and bids him read.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The first figure presents a book to Lehi; the twelve others accompany him.
unspecified_visual_details: The book’s appearance and text; the figures’ identities and appearances beyond their described brightness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The action occurs within Lehi’s vision.

title: Lehi Reads the Book
summary: As Lehi reads, he is filled with the Spirit. The book warns Jerusalem of destruction, many deaths, and captivity in Babylon.

explicit_facts.text: As Lehi reads, he is filled with the Spirit of the Lord.
Lehi reads a woe to Jerusalem and that the city and its inhabitants will be destroyed, many perishing by the sword and many carried captive into Babylon.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi reads the book given in the vision.
unspecified_visual_details: The book’s visible text and any depiction of the prophesied destruction, deaths, or captivity.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the future destruction, sword deaths, or Babylonian captivity as present events.

title: Lehi Praises the Lord
summary: After his father has read and seen many great and marvelous things, Lehi exclaims praise unto the Lord. His soul rejoices and his whole heart is filled because of what the Lord showed him.

explicit_facts.text: After reading and seeing many great and marvelous things, Lehi exclaims things unto the Lord.
Lehi praises the Lord, declaring that the Lord’s throne is high in the heavens and that his power, goodness, and mercy are over all the inhabitants of the earth.
Lehi declares that because the Lord is merciful, he will not suffer those who come unto him to perish.
Lehi’s soul rejoices and his whole heart is filled because of the things the Lord showed him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is expressing praise to the Lord.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific things Lehi read and saw.

spoken_dialogue.text: Great and marvelous are thy works, O Lord God Almighty!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

spoken_dialogue.text: Thy throne is high in the heavens, and thy power, and goodness, and mercy are over all the inhabitants of the earth, and, because thou art merciful, thou wilt not suffer those who come unto thee that they shall perish!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

title: Nephi Abridges His Father’s Record
summary: Nephi says he will not make a full account of what his father wrote. He will abridge his father’s record on plates he made with his own hands, then account for his own life.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he will not make a full account of things his father wrote, including things his father saw in visions and dreams and things he prophesied and spoke to his children.
Nephi says he will abridge his father’s record on plates he made with his own hands, then account for his own life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi making an abridgment on plates.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s location; the plates’ material and appearance; tools and method used to write.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the father, his children, visions, or dreams as present events; they are only mentioned in Nephi’s account.

title: Lehi Declares His Testimony
summary: After the Lord shows Lehi marvelous things concerning Jerusalem’s destruction, Lehi goes among the people and declares what he saw and heard; they mock him.

explicit_facts.text: After the Lord shows Lehi marvelous things concerning Jerusalem’s destruction, Lehi goes among the people and prophesies and declares what he saw and heard.
The Jews mock Lehi for testifying of their wickedness and abominations, and for what his experiences and the book manifested about the coming Messiah and redemption of the world.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi among a group of people who mock him.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities beyond the collective label, their number, exact setting, and gestures.
